title: Copying a payload prefix
statement: Let $x,p,b$ be bit strings and $m,j\in\mathbb N$. Suppose $x=p b$ and $j\le\min(m,|b|)$. Starting in state $3$ with the input head at $|p|$, unary work tape content $1^m$, work head at $m-1$, and empty output, after $j$ steps the extractor is in state $3$, with input head at $|p|+j$, the same work tape content, work head at $m-j-1$, and output equal to the first $j$ bits of $b$.
replaced: Let $p$ and $b$ be bit strings, $x = pb$, $m \in \mathbb{N}$, and $j \le \min(m, |b|)$. Then running $E$ for $j$ steps from $\Delta_x(3, |p|, m, m-1, \varepsilon)$ yields $\Delta_x(3, |p| + j, m, m - j - 1, b_{[:j]})$, where $b_{[:j]}$ is the first $j$ bits of $b$; here $E$ is the prefix-extraction machine (one work tape, states $\{0,1,2,3\}$) that counts the aligned data blocks $00$ and $11$ of a pair encoding $\langle a,b\rangle$ in unary on its work tape and then copies bits of $b$ to its output while moving its work head back along the counter, and $\Delta_x(q,i,m,h,o)$ denotes the configuration of $E$ on input $x$ in state $q$, with the input head on input position $i$ (counting from $0$), the work tape holding $1^m$ in cells $0,\dots,m-1$ and blanks elsewhere, the work head at $h$, and output $o$.
